note: Sources of founders.md and of the round-0 checks in the README, 9 November 2026, and of the README's account of the calm-air exchange at lunar gravity, from a helper's bounded review of 10 November (12 searches, 6 pages; its report, notes and full source list are on the research drive, session-tools/agents/lunar_free_convection/). read: "page read" means the source's own page was fetched and its numbers extracted; "search summary" means the figures come from a search tool's summary of the page; "repository source" is held in another sources file or record of this repository. Working notes: /media/projectspace/terluna-research/littoral-community/review/notes.md.

sources.citation: Morgan, Finnoen, Jensen, Pelabon & Jutfelt 2020. Low potential for evolutionary rescue from climate change in a tropical fish. PNAS 117(52): 33365-33372
sources.used_for: Zebrafish CTmax under selection: +0.04 +/- 0.008 C a generation, +0.22 and -0.74 C after six generations, realised heritability 0.10 and 0.24, acclimation gain 1.31 to 0.98 C, a hard upper limit suggested

sources.citation: Padfield, Yvon-Durocher, Buckling, Jennings & Yvon-Durocher 2016. Rapid evolution of metabolic traits explains thermal adaptation in phytoplankton. Ecology Letters 19: 133-142
sources.used_for: Chlorella vulgaris: high-temperature tolerance after about 100 generations by down-regulating respiration relative to photosynthesis; experiment to 33 C

sources.citation: Geerts and others 2015. Rapid evolution of thermal tolerance in the water flea Daphnia. Nature Climate Change 5: 665-668, doi:10.1038/nclimate2628
sources.used_for: Daphnia magna CTmax rose in a two-year +4 C selection experiment on 150 clones and between the 1960s and 2000s in a lake egg bank

sources.citation: GIFT tilapia genetic gains: WorldFish abstracts and archive (three generations in Malaysia, 6-13%; sixteen generations, 5-6%), Global Seafood Advocate (about 17% over the first five generations), trade press quoting WorldFish (about 10%)
sources.used_for: Nile tilapia growth gain of 5-17% a generation across reports spanning sixteen generations

sources.citation: McPhee, Jones and others 2004. Selection for increased weight at 9 months in redclaw crayfish (Cherax quadricarinatus). Aquaculture (James Cook University record 27657); Jones, McPhee and others 1997, Selection for weight gain in redclaw crayfish (record 31594); a 2022 study of 350 families
sources.used_for: Redclaw realised heritability of harvest weight 0.38 falling to 0.13 over four generations; 0.24 in fresh stock; 0.07-0.14 across 350 families; outcrossing advised

sources.citation: Vadeboncoeur and others 2003. From Greenland to green lakes: cultural eutrophication and the loss of benthic pathways in lakes. Limnology and Oceanography 48; Vadeboncoeur and others 2001, Ecology 82
sources.used_for: Periphyton 80-98% of primary production in shallow oligotrophic Greenland lakes; benthic share falls with phosphorus; epipelic algae 50-80% in Michigan lakes

sources.citation: Marshall & Junor 1981. The decline of Salvinia molesta on Lake Kariba. Hydrobiologia 83: 477-484; with the ILEC World Lake Database entry for Lake Kariba
sources.used_for: Salvinia covered 22% of Lake Kariba by 1962 and fell to 10-15%; the lake turned oligotrophic after filling; kapenta introduced from Lake Tanganyika

sources.citation: Paterson and others 2019, Can. J. Fish. Aquat. Sci. 76: 1459, as held in biosphere/ecology/sources.json
sources.used_for: New reservoirs run eutrophic for about a decade

sources.citation: van der Wal and others 2013. Invasive crayfish threaten the development of submerged macrophytes in lake restoration. PLoS ONE 8(10): e78579
sources.used_for: Lake Terra Nova: Procambarus clarkii at 150 g/m2 strongly reduced biomass and survival of Chara virgata, Elodea nuttallii and Myriophyllum spicatum in six weeks; fish and waterfowl without added effect; gut contents

sources.citation: A mesocosm study of Procambarus clarkii in temporary ponds (Hydrobiologia; reference to confirm)
sources.used_for: Macrophyte biomass about 40% less at 1 crayfish per m2 and about 80% less at 3 per m2

sources.citation: Rodriguez, Becares & Fernandez-Alaez 2003. Shift from clear to turbid phase in Lake Chozas (NW Spain) due to the introduction of American red swamp crayfish (Procambarus clarkii). Hydrobiologia 506: 421-426
sources.used_for: Lake Chozas turned from clear to turbid after the crayfish

sources.citation: Harper and others 2002 (crayfish feeding and distribution); Smart and others 2002; Hickley & Harper 2002; Britton and others 2007 (carp); Gherardi and others 2011 (23 alien species): Lake Naivasha, Kenya
sources.used_for: P. clarkii introduced 1970; crayfish and submerged plants cycle inversely; bass and tilapias fished since 1959; carp arrived 1999 and led the fishery by 2004

sources.citation: Transplanted Vallisneria nana in the Brisbane River. Journal of Freshwater Ecology 2011, doi:10.1080/02705060.2011.553925
sources.used_for: Grazing cut cover; removing exclosure fences lost the beds rapidly and completely

sources.citation: Aquiloni and others 2010. Biological control of invasive populations of crayfish: the European eel (Anguilla anguilla) as a predator of Procambarus clarkii. Biological Invasions 12: 3817-3824
sources.used_for: Eels take small and soft crayfish from behind and reduce crayfish feeding; a complement to trapping

sources.citation: Native European eels as a potential biological control for invasive crayfish. Freshwater Biology 2015, doi:10.1111/fwb.12510
sources.used_for: Eel density near carrying capacity collapsed P. clarkii populations in French ponds without eradicating them

sources.citation: Sharpe, De Leon, Gonzalez & Torchin 2017. Tropical fish community does not recover 45 years after predator introduction. Ecology 98: 412-424; Zaret & Paine 1973
sources.used_for: Lake Gatun: native littoral fish abundance 96% below its pre-introduction level 45 years after Cichla

sources.citation: Starch in Nitellopsis obtusa of Lake Koronis, Minnesota. Journal of Freshwater Ecology 2023
sources.used_for: Bulbils 42-55% starch, thallus 3-10%; carbohydrate moves into bulbils July-September

sources.citation: Adamec, turion respiration of aquatic plants (Fundamental and Applied Limnology 2011)
sources.used_for: Turions respire 2-4 times less than shoots; Q10 1.8-2.6 when dormant

sources.citation: Kuehdorf and others 2014, clonal dependence of turion formation in Spirodela polyrhiza (doi:10.1111/ppl.12065); Appenroth 2002; Mejbel & Simons 2018, Ecology and Evolution (PMC5817126)
sources.used_for: 27 clones keep different turion yields after years in culture; clonal differences in turion induction; birth order shifts turion timing

sources.citation: Hydrilla verticillata: UF/IFAS factsheet (archived); OSTI record 6640164 (adaptation to low light); Barko & Smart 1981, Ecological Monographs
sources.used_for: Grows at 1% of full sunlight; optimum 20-27 C, maximum 30 C by IFAS, good growth at 30 C in another study; tubers germinate 15-35 C and form under short days and low nutrients

sources.citation: Dark survival of freshwater algae: Journal of Japan Society on Water Environment 24: 27 (20-day dark test); Microorganisms 2023 (a year of darkness); Journal of Phycology doi:10.1111/jpy.13374 (temperature)
sources.used_for: Scenedesmus quadricauda and Melosira ambigua kept biomass through 20 dark days, Microcystis aeruginosa fell to 1% of its cells; Microcystis recovers after a year dark; warmth shortens dark survival

sources.citation: Charophytes as pioneers: Schubert and others, Ecology of charophytes: permanent pioneers and ecosystem engineers; Botany Letters 2017, doi:10.1080/23818107.2017.1393460; a Loughborough study of colonisation
sources.used_for: Often the first macrophytes in new water bodies; Chara globularis in a 9 ha reservoir 20 days after treatment; oospore banks re-establish after decades

sources.citation: Tropical charophytes: stonewort weed guide (herbiguide.com.au); Anderson & Lommasson 1956 on Chara zeylanica; Chara braunii studies (J. Freshwater Ecology 2023; Aust. J. Bot. BT97104); Vieira & Necchi 2003 on Brazilian stream species
sources.used_for: Tropical Characeae survive in waters to about 30 C; no growth data at 30-35 C found; Chara photosynthesis peaked at 10-15 C and dark respiration rose to 25 C in the Brazilian study

sources.citation: Azolla: FAO review i1141e02 citing Cagauan & Pullin 1991; Plants 2022 (PMC9032100)
sources.used_for: Heat tolerance ranked from A. mexicana to A. filiculoides; optimum near 25 C, A. mexicana about 30 C; doubling 2.16 d at best, 3.7-9.5 d outdoors; 53-1,000 kg N per ha

sources.citation: Kolbe and others 2004. Genetic variation increases during biological invasion by a Cuban lizard. Nature 431: 177-181; Dlugosch & Parker 2008, Molecular Ecology 17: 431-449
sources.used_for: At least eight introductions and more variation than in the native range; multiple introductions raise diversity across invasions

sources.citation: Meier, Marques, Mwaiko, Wagner, Excoffier & Seehausen 2017. Ancient hybridization fuels rapid cichlid fish adaptive radiations. Nature Communications 8: 14363
sources.used_for: About 700 species of the Lake Victoria Region Superflock descend from a hybrid swarm of two lineages

sources.citation: Barluenga, Stolting, Salzburger, Muschick & Meyer 2006. Sympatric speciation in Nicaraguan crater lake cichlid fish. Nature 439: 719-723; reply to Schliewen and others 2006
sources.used_for: Amphilophus zaliosus arose in Lake Apoyo within less than about 10,000 years; the sympatric reading is disputed

sources.citation: Gutekunst and others 2018, Nature Ecology & Evolution, with the authors' account "Invasion of the clones"
sources.used_for: Marbled crayfish: one all-female triploid clone; Madagascar range from about 1,000 to over 100,000 km2 in ten years; sold as food

sources.citation: Redclaw in the Zambezi basin: Biological Invasions 2023 (Rufford Foundation PDF); Socioeconomic impacts of Australian redclaw crayfish (White Rose eprint 198654); Mongabay 2025
sources.used_for: Wild in the Kafue 2001 and Lake Kariba 2002; nearly the whole 1,600 km Kafue; Kariba gillnet fishers lose about 212 t a year

sources.citation: Redclaw thermal limits: Iheringia (SciELO) paper; CICESE thesis, Baja California Sur; CSIRO Marine and Freshwater Research MF9900735; a review of tropical crustaceans (PMC10907542)
sources.used_for: Lethal at 10 and 36 C; growth optimum 25-30 C; CTmax 36 to 42 C with acclimation 20 to 32 C; preferred 28.7 C

sources.citation: Procambarus clarkii: Buckle and others 1996, Rev. Biol. Trop. 44; Effects of thermal stress on growth and reproduction of Procambarus clarkii, Animals 2026, 16(3): 495; University of Florence abstract; Auburn MSc thesis 2024
sources.used_for: Preferendum 23.4 C; growth optimum 20-25 C, reproduction 18-22 C; adults to 37 C; burrowing follows the groundwater

sources.citation: Corbicula fluminea: Johnson & McMahon 1998, CJFAS (f98-030); Matthews & McMahon 1999; Virginia Tech thesis on the New River
sources.used_for: High mortality near 36 C; LT50 of 144-216 h under low oxygen at 25 C

sources.citation: Melanoides tuberculata: Acta Limnologica Brasiliensia (temperature and salinity tolerance); NeoBiota 2025; Potential for emergence of foodborne trematodiases transmitted by an introduced snail, medRxiv 2022.01.21.22269661 (preprint)
sources.used_for: Tolerates 16-37 C, optimum 29-34 C; first reproduction about 275 d at 25 C; first host of at least 11 human-infecting trematodes; infected snails at 19 of 41 Californian fishing sites

sources.citation: Physa acuta life tables: National Academy Science Letters 2018, doi:10.1007/s40009-018-0709-z; a West Bengal cohort study 2017
sources.used_for: Generation about 47 d; maturity at 28-42 d; higher temperature and salinity tolerance than a native competitor; survives drying

sources.citation: Neocaridina davidi: temperature and offspring sex ratio (Turkish study); temperature and reproduction (Argentine study, Acta Zoologica doi:10.1111/azo.12336)
sources.used_for: Offspring 80% female at 20 C, 18% at 26 C; 20 C depresses reproduction against 24 and 28 C

sources.citation: Daphnia lumholtzi: Lennon and others 2001; Engel & Tollrian 2009 (PMC2674494); Mantovano and others 2021
sources.used_for: Tropical origin; spread through North American reservoirs in about thirty years in the summer thermal niche; inducible spines against fish

sources.citation: Sinanodonta woodiana: a 2012 host experiment (Institute of Vertebrate Biology PDF); NeoBiota 103 (2025), doi:10.3897/neobiota.103.160537
sources.used_for: Completes development on all eight fish species tested; larvae on all eight wild species sampled; lowers a native mussel's metamorphosis on shared hosts

sources.citation: Limnoperna fortunei: Biofouling study of upper lethal temperature; reviews of its hypoxia tolerance and Pantanal die-offs (CONICET; EMBRAPA)
sources.used_for: More heat-resistant than Dreissena polymorpha; withstands 0.5 mg/L of oxygen for long periods and dies in the Pantanal oxygen crashes; fouls intakes

sources.citation: Leiopotherapon unicolor: desertfishes.org species account (citing Llewellyn 1973, Glover 1990); Fishes of Australia species 694; FishBase mirror
sources.used_for: Waters of 5-44 C; LD50 about 39 C; 24,000-113,200 eggs; 16.6 km overland in six hours; diet of invertebrates, crustaceans, molluscs, fish

sources.citation: Scortum barcoo: Queensland Government aquaculture pages; Fishes of Australia species 701
sources.used_for: Tolerates water to 40 C by two accounts, 12-34 C by a farming guide; spawns in summer floods above 23 C; omnivore taking crustaceans and molluscs

sources.citation: Oreochromis niloticus: FAO cultured aquatic species fact sheet (excerpt); Global Invasive Species Database; Campos-Mendoza and others 2004 (Stirling record 1893/31035); Rad and others 2006; Martinez-Chavez and others 2021
sources.used_for: Lethal at 11-12 and 42 C, preferred 31-36 C; maturity at 5-6 months; under continuous light the second-highest fecundity and short spawning intervals of four regimes

sources.citation: Astronotus ocellatus: Florida Museum species profile; Hydrobiologia 2016, doi:10.1007/s10750-016-2740-8
sources.used_for: Diet includes crayfish and snails; lower lethal about 12.9 C; southern Everglades waters 13.2-35.5 C; biparental; mature at about a year

sources.citation: Cichla: reproduction in Brazilian reservoirs (Rev. Biol. Trop. 59(2); J. Fish Biology doi:10.1111/jfb.14618); Swingle 1966, SEAFWA (temperature tolerance and a pond test)
sources.used_for: Reproductive activity through almost the whole year; fingerlings die below 61 F

sources.citation: Clarias gariepinus early life: Aquatic Living Resources 1995 (alr95423)
sources.used_for: Early-life thermal zone 18.9-33.2 C; embryos die above about 35 C

sources.citation: Wood and others 2003 (Potamotrygon in Rio Negro blackwater); Gonzalez and others 1998, 2002; Gonzalez, Wilson & Wood 2005, Ionoregulation in tropical fishes from ion-poor, acidic blackwaters, Fish Physiology 21
sources.used_for: Rio Negro water holds 30 umol/L or less of Na+, Cl- and Ca2+; its fishes keep their salts there; sodium uptake affinity differs by lineage

sources.citation: Miller MJ, Beljaars ACM, Palmer TN 1992. The sensitivity of the ECMWF model to the parameterization of evaporation from the tropical oceans. Journal of Climate 5: 418-434
sources.used_for: The free-convection transfer over water in unstable air, 0.0016 dtheta^(1/3) m/s, from tank experiments; held in research/studies/lake_oxygen/sources.json and derived in climate/gcm/README.md (26 October), which scales it by the cube root of gravity over pressure

sources.citation: Beljaars 1995, as the climate lane cites it for the gust in the surface exchange (climate/gcm/README.md, "Beljaars's gust in PlaSim's surface transfer over four years (28 October)"); the paper was not opened for this study
sources.used_for: The gust of the boundary layer's large eddies in the surface exchange, w* = (g/theta_v h B)^(1/3), as climate/gcm/README.md records it (28 October); the review's inference that the transfer then goes as the square root of gravity times the layer's depth at a given contrast

sources.citation: Funfschilling D, Brown E, Nikolaenko A, Ahlers G 2005. Heat transport by turbulent Rayleigh-Benard convection in cylindrical samples with aspect ratio one and larger. Journal of Fluid Mechanics, doi:10.1017/S0022112005005057
sources.used_for: Water, Prandtl number 4.38: the effective exponent of the heat transfer on the Rayleigh number rises from 0.28 near 1e8 to 0.333 near 7e10 (the arXiv abstract, read by the helper)

sources.citation: Jiang H, Zhu X, Wang D, Huisman SG, Sun C 2020. Supergravitational turbulent thermal convection. Science Advances 6: eabb8676
sources.used_for: A rotating annulus of water at 5-60 g: the heat transfer follows the Rayleigh-number law with an exponent of 0.27 +/- 0.01 below 1e10, a third near 1e10 and more above 4e10; the Coriolis force keeps the flow nearly two-dimensional (full text, read by the helper)

sources.citation: Lotto MA, Johnson KM, Nie CW, Klaus DM 2017. The impact of reduced gravity on free convective heat transfer from a finite, flat, vertical plate. Microgravity Science and Technology 29(5): 371-379, doi:10.1007/s12217-017-9555-8
sources.used_for: Parabolic flights averaging 0.05 g: Nusselt number 19.05 +/- 1.41 against 18.90 +/- 0.63 from the Churchill-Chu correlation (N = 13), 61% less heat transfer than at 1 g; laminar by its Nusselt number (the abstract, read by the helper)

sources.citation: Tillman and others 1994. The Martian atmospheric planetary boundary layer stability, fluxes, spectra, and similarity. Report, as its record gives it; a journal version was not checked
sources.used_for: Viking Lander 2's data: Earth's surface-layer similarity theory applies to Mars

sources.citation: Spiga A, Forget F, Lewis SR, Hinson DP 2010. Structure and dynamics of the convective boundary layer on Mars as inferred from large-eddy simulations and remote-sensing measurements. Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society 136: 414-428
sources.used_for: Large-eddy simulations at 3.72 m/s2 reproduce the boundary-layer depths measured by radio occultation, up to 9 km; the surface-flux convective velocity is less relevant there, since infrared heating within the air leaves the surface flux near 0.15 of the layer's maximum (the paper's text, read by the helper)

sources.citation: Sears DWG, Moore SR 2005. On laboratory simulation and the evaporation rate of water on Mars. Geophysical Research Letters 32, doi:10.1029/2005GL023443
sources.used_for: Water at 0 C and 7 mbar in a chamber at Earth gravity: 1.01 +/- 0.19 mm/h, and 0.73 +/- 0.14 mm/h after the correction to Mars gravity, the cube root of 0.38

sources.citation: Luspay-Kuti A and others 2012. Experimental simulations of CH4 evaporation on Titan. Geophysical Research Letters, doi:10.1029/2012GL054003
sources.used_for: Methane at 94 K and 1.5 bar in a chamber at Earth gravity: (3.1 +/- 0.6)e-4 kg m-2 s-1, and (1.6 +/- 0.3)e-4 after the correction to Titan gravity, the cube root of 0.14
